A TikTok user calling themselves Aqua Traveller claims to be from 2609 and says robots will take over the world

07:00, 12 Oct 2026Updated 09:48, 12 Oct 2026

A cryptic social media user, claiming to be a "time traveller from the year 2609", has made bold claims about when " robots will take over" Earth. The enigmatic 'Aqua Traveller', who posts under the handle @aqua_time_traveller, has amassed over 1,800 followers by sharing their foreboding predictions about the future - ranging from the discovery of new planets to catastrophic natural disasters.

‌

‌

In their revelation, the self-proclaimed time-jumper claims to know the dates of some significant upcoming events - including the precise date of the robot rebellion.

‌

In the video, which has racked up more than 2,700 views, they said: "These big events and their dates... February 17, 2103, robots are officially going to take over the world."

‌

TikTok users were left scratching their heads as they flocked to the comments section to express their bewilderment and share their thoughts on the alarming prophecy.

One viewer said: "February 17 is my birthday but the year.." Another simply responded: "Yeah, definitely." A third added with: "Totally."

However, other users were particularly disturbed by another prediction in the clip, which claimed that " dogs will be extinct on 9 December 2046."

One horrified user said: "The dog one has to be fake." Another wrote: "I don't believe. "Ok, how are dogs gonna go extinct?" a third queried.

‌

This comes after another alleged " time traveller from 2671" suggested that parents will have the ability to genetically modify their children by the end of 2023.

Eno Alaric, who goes by the handle @theradianttimetraveller, has amassed over 26,000 followers by sharing alerts about alleged upcoming occurrences.

The content creator has previously issued warnings concerning twin planets alongside Earth, extraterrestrial encounters and even gateways opening to alternative dimensions.

But now, the self-proclaimed time-hopper has declared that parents are merely months away from being able to select optimal genes for their offspring to eliminate hereditary disorders and even determine their physical traits.
